findings.problem: LeaseWorkflow uses String for status and separate bool flags (is_validated, is_sent) instead of an enum typestate, allowing illegal states like status="sent" with is_sent=false, or status="pending" with is_sent=true.
findings.failure_mode: Any code branch checking only is_sent or only status can observe inconsistent state, leading to missed validations, duplicate sends, or incorrect audit trails.
findings.fix: Replace status: String, is_validated: bool, and is_sent: bool with a single LeaseStatus enum (e.g., Pending, Validated, Sent) and remove redundant bool fields. The type system enforces exactly one state at a time.

findings.problem: id: String is a bare primitive with no domain invariants. sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> is a raw epoch milliseconds without a dedicated newtype.
findings.failure_mode: Invalid IDs (empty, malformed) and invalid timestamps (zero, future-dated, negative duration) pass through the core undetected. Comparisons on raw u64 epoch values are error-prone without a typed wrapper.
findings.fix: Introduce a LeaseId newtype (e.g., struct LeaseId(String)) with a fallible constructor that validates non-empty and domain constraints. Introduce a TimestampMs newtype for sent_at_epoch_ms with a fallible constructor.

findings.problem: mark_sent takes and returns an owned LeaseWorkflow by value, mutating fields in place. There is no typestate or invariant enforcement — any caller can mutate status, is_validated, or is_sent arbitrarily.
findings.failure_mode: Callers can transition from Sent back to Pending, clear is_sent, or corrupt validation state, bypassing any intended workflow ordering (pending -> validated -> sent).
findings.fix: Make LeaseWorkflow fields private. Provide a fallible constructor that enforces preconditions (e.g., can only mark_sent from Validated state). Use enum typestate so transitions are compile-enforced: fn mark_sent(self) -> Result<LeaseWorkflow, TransitionError>.

findings.problem: mark_sent uses .to_string() allocation on every call to set status="sent", creating an owned String in the core instead of using an enum or borrowed representation.
findings.failure_mode: Unnecessary heap allocation on every state transition. Combined with the String-based status, this also means any string literal can be assigned (e.g., "SENT", "Sent", ""), not just the canonical "sent".
findings.fix: Replace status: String with a LeaseStatus enum. The mark_sent function returns a LeaseStatus::Sent variant without any allocation.

findings.problem: is_validated: bool and is_sent: bool are redundant flags that duplicate information already partly encoded in status: String. Three independent booleans/String fields create 2^3 * N possible values where only a few are valid.
findings.failure_mode: State space explosion: 3 independent fields yield 2^3=8 combinations of bools times N status strings, most of which represent impossible or contradictory workflows. This makes partial-application bugs likely.
findings.fix: Collapse into a single LeaseStatus enum with variants that encode the full workflow state. Remove is_validated and is_sent entirely. The enum makes illegal states unrepresentable by construction.

findings.problem: All fields of LeaseWorkflow are pub, allowing external mutation of internal state without any validation or workflow guards.
findings.failure_mode: Any module can set item.status = "anything" or item.is_validated = false, breaking invariants without any error type or workflow enforcement.
findings.fix: Make all fields private (remove pub). Provide a private constructor or a fallible new() method. Expose only the data needed externally via getters or a non-mutable snapshot.

residual_risk: Static review only; no commands run. The crate has fundamental type discipline violations: primitive obsession (String status, bare bool flags), no typestate enforcement, no newtyped domain values, and fully mutable public fields. These are BLOCKERs that must be resolved before the crate can be considered Holzman-compliant. The core has no pure calculation layer and the struct cannot represent valid workflow invariants at compile time.
